content.title: Marge Roberts Park Renovations
content.summary: Marge Roberts Park has officially reopened to the public following extensive renovations that began in 2021. The project included updates to playground equipment, sidewalks, and landscaping, as well as the addition of new features such as an adventure trail, artificial turf mounds, and improved accessibility, culminating in a ribbon-cutting ceremony on October 7, 2025.
content.body:
## Marge Roberts Park is now open

Marge Roberts Park is now open to the public. The City celebrated the reopening of the park with a ribbon cutting event on Tuesday, Oct. 7, 2025.

The City greatly appreciates everyone's patience and understanding the past few months as the final touches were made to allow us to safely open the park to the public.

## Project Background

The Marge Roberts Park project began in 2021 as one of the City's [Taking Lasting Care (TLC) playground renovations](http://860). Because several other areas were also in need of repair, the City instead began a major overhaul of the entire park.

Along with the aging playground equipment, the park had upheaved sidewalks, deteriorating retaining walls, overgrown vegetation, and an outdated irrigation system. Construction began in the fall of 2024, and the park was opened to the public in the fall of 2025.

Marge Roberts Park is [located at 5881 Miller St.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/GEcNjSKztCSGPRYU8), across 58th Ave. from Lutz Sports Complex.

## New Park Features

The City hired Stream Landscape Architecture and Planning to help revitalize the park, bring it up to code, improve accessibility and expand its use for the broader community. The park improvements include:

- New nature-themed play equipment
- Adventure trail with play elements
- Artificial turf mounds
- New benches and picnic tables
- Expanded basketball court
- Concrete loop trail with parallel soft surface path
- Native landscaping around the periphery of the park
- Updated irrigation
- New water tap
- Improved landscaping (in alignment with the City's low-water and low-maintenance goals)

## Project Timeline

- Spring 2021: Feedback collected from the community through Speak Up Arvada surveys
- Spring and Summer 2023: Construction documents completed and bid out to contractors
- Fall and Winter 2023: Bidding and contract awarded
- Summer/Fall 2024: Construction began
- Oct. 7, 2025: Park open to the public!

## Public Engagement

In March 2021, the City team conducted a survey on Speak Up Arvada asking residents to weigh in on the playground elements and theme. Survey responses are being used to inform the new playground designs.

## Park History

Marge Roberts Park was first purchased by the City with Arvada's share of Open Space funds in August 1979. Originally named Holder Park, it was renamed in 1990 for Arvada resident Marge Roberts, who led a neighborhood group in the park's redesign. The park was previously updated in 2004.

Marge Roberts was active in several local non-profit organizations, earning her the [Arvada Chamber's "Woman of the Year" honors](https://www.arvadachamber.org/chamberawards/) in 1976 for her service to the community.
